sample_unit: informed consent documents from AI clinical trials

links.outcome: Consent document length and readability (SMOG) in AI trials
links.effect: Only 14% (n=16) of ICs met dual criteria of brevity (<15,000 characters) and readability (SMOG <13). Higher-risk trials did not show improved readability (Spearman P>.05).
links.quote: Only 14% (n=16) of ICs met the dual criteria of brevity (<15,000 characters) and readability (Simple Measure of Gobbledygook <13).

links.outcome: Disclosure of AI type or intended use in consent documents
links.effect: 66/114 (58%) of ICs failed to disclose the AI type or its intended use; 18.4% (n=21) omitted risks entirely.
links.quote: More than half (66/114, 58%) of ICs failed to disclose the AI type or its intended use, and 18.4% (n=21) omitted risks entirely.

links.outcome: Data handling after participant withdrawal in consent documents
links.effect: 51 (44.7%) ICs gave no information, 30 (26.3%) specified data destruction, 29 (25.4%) allowed continued use, only 4 (3.5%) offered participants a choice.
links.quote: Data handling protocols after participant withdrawal were inconsistent: 51 (44.7%) ICs provided no information, 30 (26.3%) specified data destruction, 29 (25.4%) allowed continued use, and only 4 (3.5%) offered participants a choice.

links.outcome: Visual aid use and association with reading difficulty in consent documents
links.effect: Only 11.4% (n=13) of ICs included visual aids; inclusion not correlated with lower reading difficulty.
links.quote: Only 11.4% (n=13) of ICs included visual aids, and their inclusion was not correlated with lower reading difficulty.

unlisted_practices: Minimum Requirements for Informed Consent in AI-related Clinical Trials framework
Consistency between trial registry entries and informed consent AI descriptions

screen.reason: Evaluates the completeness, readability, and presence of AI disclosures in informed consent documents from 114 clinical trials evaluating AI interventions.
